title: One product. Two ways to tell its story.

panels.title: 01 / A product worth showing
panels.caption: OWNER + COFFEE / A REAL STARTING POINT
panels.action: At a modest, cared-for work counter, one Filipino business owner places their bottled coffee beside a phone. They line up a simple product photo. A small packing area suggests an operating business; no staged crisis or invented sales numbers.
panels.camera: Close on the bottle touching the counter; ease back just enough to include the owner's hands and face. Keep the bottle and expression central for mobile.
panels.sound: Room tone, a physical bottle contact and phone shutter. Natural Taglish intent may enter after exact dialogue review; no voice command to the app.
panels.proof: Externally produced owner scene. Casting, location and new coffee brand are proposals, not approved identities. This exact bottle/photo becomes the shared input.
panels.transition: Match the photographed bottle to that same image on the real Grifon upload screen.

panels.title: 02 / Give Grifon the real brief
panels.caption: ACTUAL UI CAPTURE TO BE RECORDED
panels.action: Over the owner's shoulder, the product photo enters the actual Grifon workflow. Show the business brief being supplied through real controls, then isolate one readable piece of information. No invented chat interface.
panels.camera: Begin with the owner using the screen, then cut to a legible screen capture. Reframe the relevant control rather than shrink an entire desktop onto a phone.
panels.sound: Tactile input sounds; a restrained musical pulse starts. Leave speech space. Edited waiting periods must be apparent so the sequence does not promise instant generation.
panels.proof: Real interface recording with run ID, account tier, inputs and settings retained. Screen here is a diagram placeholder, not verified UI or a working prototype.
panels.transition: A visible time ellipsis leads to the actual plan. The bottle image stays in the same visual position across the cut.

panels.title: 03 / The idea becomes a plan
panels.caption: PHOTO > AD PLAN > TWO CREATIVE DIRECTIONS
panels.action: Reveal a readable excerpt from the actual coffee ad plan. The owner reviews the hook and scenes. The accepted gold ribbon guides attention from the photo to the plan, then the living studio opens around that work as an editorial presentation.
panels.camera: Controlled lateral move along one idea at a time. A brief wider studio composition supplies scale, then stop moving to let the real plan be read.
panels.sound: The pulse gains texture as the plan becomes clear; one soft transition accent on the studio reveal. No wall-to-wall whooshes or borrowed reference audio.
panels.proof: The plan is actual Grifon output. The surrounding Blender studio and ribbon motion are external launch production. Show the move to paid video creation clearly before the sample sequence; no implication that Free includes videos.
panels.transition: The studio display fills the frame, then a clean cut enters the UGC export. The ribbon stops before the proof begins.

panels.title: 04 / First, make it feel human
panels.caption: GRIFON SAMPLE AD / UGC / PAID PLAN
panels.action: Play an uninterrupted excerpt of the real UGC export: the same coffee product in a believable human presentation. Proposed preference: reuse the owner's approved identity if the ordinary product path supports it; otherwise clearly cast a separate presenter later.
panels.camera: Use the export's actual camera and framing. Keep the face, product and approved English subtitles readable; preserve the full source frame rather than crop away flaws.
panels.sound: Let the export's original voice and sound lead. Duck the wrapper score. Natural Taglish performance and intelligibility must pass listening review.
panels.proof: Original Grifon UGC export, pending generation. Keep the label 'Grifon sample ad' visible and identify paid-plan output nearby. No external face, voice or label repairs inside the proof.
panels.transition: End on the product where the source permits. Clean cut to the cinematic export; no invented morph between outputs.

panels.title: 05 / Then, give it presence
panels.caption: GRIFON SAMPLE AD / CINEMATIC / PAID PLAN
panels.action: Play an uninterrupted excerpt of the actual cinematic export. Proposed target: a disciplined product reveal with consistent label, coffee fill and believable material highlights. Let one strong image carry the moment.
panels.camera: Use motion the actual Grifon export achieves. Do not promise a particular orbit, liquid simulation or native 4K. The studio candidate cannot substitute for this sample.
panels.sound: Preserve the export's sound where present. Any wrapper score remains clearly an assembly layer and never implies an unproduced product capability. Exact treatment awaits the audiovisual brief.
panels.proof: Original cinematic Grifon export from the same approved product master. Preserve input hashes, ordinary tier/settings, roll history and cost. Reproduce a selected result before making a typical-quality claim.
panels.transition: Pull back from playback into the owner's real review screen as an external edit, returning to the starting work counter.

panels.title: 06 / Back to the owner
panels.caption: ONE OWNER / TWO RESULTS / ONE NEXT STEP
panels.action: The owner compares the two completed ads and checks the bottle beside the screen. A quiet, satisfied reaction closes the loop without a testimonial or promised sales outcome. Resolve to a clear free ad-plan invitation on the existing website.
panels.camera: Return to the opening composition with the results now visible. Hold the closing layout for comprehension; the final hold length remains open. Keep the website CTA accessible outside playback.
panels.sound: Return to the room tone; the score resolves gently. No obligatory sales voice-over. Silent viewing must still explain the input, result and next action.
panels.proof: Externally produced reaction plus real exports on screen. Proposed English CTA: 'Build my free ad plan'. Supporting copy: 'One free ad-plan preview a month. No card required. Finished videos require a paid plan.' Recheck runtime before release.
panels.transition: Gold ribbon settles into the existing website visual language. End card resolves without hiding the page's next action or requiring the film to finish.
